The test image shows corn plants with:
- Whole-plant death/premature senescence
- Stalk lodging/collapse of multiple plants
- Shredded, dead brown leaves/tissue
- Stalks appear to have broken or collapsed at the base

This pattern strongly suggests stalk rot. The shredded stalk appearance and lodging pattern narrows it to Diplodia, Anthracnose, Charcoal, or Fusarium stalk rot. Let me view a reference image.

The Anthracnose stalk rot reference shows:
- **Bottom-right panel**: Field view with lodged/collapsed plants — very similar to the test image
- **Top-right panel**: Shredded pith with shiny black rind discoloration
- **Bottom-left panel**: Close-up of characteristic shiny black stalk rind

The test image matches Anthracnose stalk rot well:
- Multiple plants showing complete collapse/lodging in the field
- Shredded stalk tissue and premature whole-plant death
- The field-level pattern of dead, lodged plants is consistent with the reference bottom-right panel
- The stalk bases appear to have failed, causing the classic lodging

The shiny black rind discoloration (diagnostic for Anthracnose) would be visible on closer inspection of the stalks, but the field-level presentation of multiple lodged, completely dead plants is characteristic.
